errors_in_wrong_drawing: [substituent_position, high] On the left benzene ring the reference has AcNH para (1,4) to the sulfonyl S; the wrong drawing places AcNH on the lower-left vertex, meta (1,3) to the S-bearing carbon.
review_notes: Wrong drawing moves AcNH from para to meta relative to SO2 on the left benzene; everything else matches. Corrected drawing restores para and matches the reference. Cursive Bn in both handwritten copies is readable and not counted as an error.

errors_in_wrong_drawing: [connectivity, high] In the reference the CH2CH2CH2-NH-C(=O)NH2 side chain is attached (solid wedge) to the citrulline alpha carbon, which sits between the amide NH and the C(=O)NH-aryl. In the wrong drawing the side chain's wedge bond ends on the amide nitrogen (N with H below) instead, and the alpha carbon is drawn as an unsubstituted CH2 between that N and the C(=O)NH-aryl. The N is left with three carbon bonds plus an H. | [stereochemistry, high] Because the side chain was moved, the reference's solid wedge at the citrulline alpha-carbon stereocentre is gone. The wedge now points at the amide nitrogen, and the alpha carbon (drawn as CH2) has no stereochemistry. The iPr wedge is still correct.
review_notes: Wrong drawing: the citrulline side chain (with its wedge) is attached to the amide N instead of the alpha carbon, which becomes a plain CH2. The corrected drawing matches the reference. Its use of aromatic circles in place of Kekule bonds and the gamma-like r in iPr are only style. The wrong drawing writes the urea NH2 on the right ('NH2' rather than 'H2N'); this is just orientation and was not counted. Transcriber_2's 'wrong' transcription describes an unrelated quinoline and was ignored.

errors_in_wrong_drawing: [substituent_position, high] The reference has Cl para (1,4) to the triazolone N1 attachment on the chlorophenyl ring (4-chlorophenyl); the wrong drawing places Cl meta (1,3) to the N1 attachment (Cl on the left vertex, N1 bond from the upper-right vertex, one carbon between them), giving a 3-chlorophenyl isomer.
review_notes: Wrong drawing puts Cl meta instead of para to the triazolone N on the chlorophenyl ring; the corrected drawing restores para and otherwise matches the reference. Both handwritten versions draw benzene rings as circles instead of alternating double bonds (same compound; not counted as an error).

errors_in_wrong_drawing: [substituent_position, high] Reference attaches the CH2-piperidine linker at carbazole C3 (right benzo ring carbon para to the N-bearing fusion carbon C9a); the wrong drawing attaches it at C2 (the ring carbon meta to C9a, two bonds from it along the top edge). | [abbreviation_changed, medium] Reference N-substituent is the abbreviation 'Et'; the wrong drawing expands it to 'CH2CH3'. | [abbreviation_changed, medium] Reference indane C1 substituent is the abbreviation 'NHAc'; the wrong drawing expands it to NH-C(=O)-CH3 with explicit C, CH3 and =O.
review_notes: Wrong drawing moves the CH2 linker from carbazole C3 to C2 and expands Et and NHAc. Corrected drawing restores C3, Et and NHAc with matching stereo; the H in NHAc is slightly odd but readable.

errors_in_wrong_drawing: [substituent_position, high] Reference central benzene is para (1,4)-disubstituted: piperazine N and the O-CH2 ether on opposite vertices. In the wrong drawing the piperazine N is on the upper-left vertex and the O on the upper-right vertex, i.e. meta (1,3) positions.
issues_in_corrected_drawing: [legibility, low] Both Cl labels on the dichlorophenyl ring are written in a loose cursive form that is readable in context but less clear than the reference Cl.
review_notes: Wrong drawing puts the piperazine and the O-CH2 meta on the central benzene instead of para. Everything else (rings, Cl positions, imidazole, both hashed bonds) matches. Corrected drawing restores para; only a minor cursive-Cl legibility note.

errors_in_wrong_drawing: [substituent_position, high] The reference has the CH2-C(=O)-N(3,3-difluoropiperidinyl) group at indole C5 (benzo-ring carbon para to the N-bearing fusion carbon C7a, meta to C3a). The wrong drawing attaches it to the benzo-ring carbon directly adjacent to the N-bearing fusion carbon (indole C7).
review_notes: Wrong drawing moves the CH2C(=O)-difluoropiperidine amide from indole C5 to C7; everything else matches. The wrong photo is cropped at the right edge with an unreadable stub at C5, which does not change the finding. Corrected drawing has the group at C5 and matches the reference; Cl and Ac are written loosely but readable.

errors_in_wrong_drawing: [connectivity, high] Six-membered ring heteroatoms rearranged: the reference ring is N1-C2(COOtBu)-N3-C4(fusion, bears N9)-C5-C6(NH2); the wrong drawing has the two N atoms adjacent (N-N bond) at the top, and the ester-bearing carbon sits next to the fusion carbon where N3 should be, so COOtBu is no longer on the carbon between the two ring nitrogens. | [abbreviation_changed, medium] Reference label COOtBu is expanded in the wrong drawing to COO-C(CH3)3 (tBu written out as C with three CH3). | [abbreviation_changed, medium] Reference condensed label H2N is expanded to an explicit H-N-H drawn vertically with bonds on the left six-ring carbon.
issues_in_corrected_drawing: [legibility, low] The hashed bond from cyclohexane C4 stops short of the line leading to CO2H, leaving a small gap; the CH2 vertex (reference CH2-CO2H) is readable from the change in direction but slightly ambiguous.
review_notes: Wrong drawing turns the pyrimidine part of the purine into an N-N ring with the ester moved next to the fusion carbon, and expands tBu and H2N. Corrected drawing matches the reference; only a small gap at the CH2-CO2H hashed bond. Both handwritten copies use an aromatic circle in the six-ring instead of the reference Kekule bonds; treated as acceptable depiction.

errors_in_wrong_drawing: [substituent_position, high] In the reference the alkene carbon is attached to C2 of the tetramethyltetralin (an aromatic carbon one CH away from the ring-fusion carbon). In the wrong drawing it is attached to the aromatic carbon directly adjacent to the ring-fusion carbon (C1, peri to a gem-dimethyl carbon). | [abbreviation_changed, medium] The reference label EtOOC on the left benzene ring is expanded in the wrong drawing to a drawn carbonyl (C=O with the C written as a letter) plus an OEt label, so the reference abbreviation is not preserved.
review_notes: The wrong drawing has two problems: EtOOC is expanded to C(=O)OEt, and the vinyl group sits on the tetralin carbon next to the ring fusion instead of one carbon further along. The ring-position call comes from a freehand hexagon, but the edge from the attachment vertex to the fusion carbon looks clear. Please confirm which error was the intended one; it decides the primary category. The corrected drawing matches the reference; its O that looks like a D is only cosmetic.

errors_in_wrong_drawing: [substituent_position, high] The reference has EtOOC on C2 of the five-membered ring, directly adjacent to N(Ac); the wrong drawing places EtOOC on C3 (the carbon bonded to the lower ring-fusion carbon), with an unsubstituted CH2 between N(Ac) and the EtOOC-bearing carbon.
review_notes: Wrong drawing moves the ethyl ester from C2 (next to N-Ac) to C3 of the five-membered ring; the pyridine N and OMe positions are right. The corrected drawing puts EtOOC back on C2 and matches the reference. Aromatic ring drawn as a circle in both handwritten versions (same compound).

errors_in_wrong_drawing: [wrong_atom_or_label, high] Reference six-membered fused ring is a pyridine with ring N adjacent to the fusion carbon bearing the lactam N (7-aza position); the wrong drawing omits this N and draws an all-carbon benzene ring, so the 7-azaoxindole becomes an oxindole. | [abbreviation_changed, medium] Reference para substituent on the benzyl ring is the abbreviation 'OMe'; the wrong drawing expands it to 'OCH3'.
review_notes: Wrong drawing leaves out the pyridine N (drawn as benzene) and writes OMe as OCH3. Corrected drawing restores the ring N in the right place and uses OMe; everything else matches.

errors_in_wrong_drawing: [substituent_position, high] Reference benzene has the triazolyl para to the NH (and meta to OEt). Wrong drawing attaches the triazolyl to the vertex adjacent to the OEt carbon, i.e. ortho to OEt and meta to NH (1,2,3-trisubstituted pattern). | [connectivity, high] Reference partially saturated ring of the bicycle is N-CH2-C8a and N-CH=CH-C4a. Wrong drawing has N-CH2-CH2-C8a (two sp3 carbons on the C8a side) and N-CH=C4a, with the double bond going to the aromatic fusion carbon; ring atoms are arranged differently and the CH=CH double bond is misplaced. | [abbreviation_changed, medium] Reference abbreviations Me (on triazole N), MeO (azetidine) and OEt (benzene) are expanded to CH3, CH3O and O-CH2-CH3. | [other, medium] Methyl groups drawn as unlabelled skeletal lines in the reference (two on azetidine C2, one on the pyridine ring) are written out as explicit CH3 labels, so the reference notation is not preserved.
issues_in_corrected_drawing: [missing_atom_or_group, high] Reference has a 4-methyl-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl (three ring N: N-Me plus an N=N side). Corrected drawing's five-membered ring has only two N (N-Me and one other N); the ring atom adjacent to the attachment carbon on the lower side is drawn as carbon with a C=C double bond instead of N, giving an imidazole. | [legibility, low] Azetidine C2 quaternary carbon is drawn as two straight lines crossing (methyl line running straight through to N), making the vertex harder to read than in the reference.
review_notes: Wrong has several errors: triazole moved to meta of NH (ortho to OEt), bicycle ring atoms rearranged (CH2-CH2 / CH=C fusion), and Me/MeO/OEt and methyl lines written out as CH3. The corrected drawing fixes these but its triazole has only two ring N (drawn as an imidazole), so it is not fully correct.

errors_in_wrong_drawing: [substituent_position, high] The reference has OPh para (1,4) to the CH2 side chain on the benzene ring. The wrong drawing puts OPh at the top vertex and the CH2 at the lower-left vertex, i.e. meta (1,3).
review_notes: Wrong drawing has OPh meta to the side chain instead of para. Labels, hashed bond and chain otherwise match. Corrected drawing restores para and matches the reference; handwriting is loose but readable.

errors_in_wrong_drawing: [ring_size_or_fusion, high] The 3,4-difluorophenyl ring of the reference (six-membered) is drawn as a five-membered ring with three double bonds; one ring vertex is missing between the NH-bearing carbon and the F-bearing carbon, so as drawn the two F atoms sit ortho and meta to the NH carbon instead of meta and para.
review_notes: Wrong drawing's difluorophenyl ring has only five vertices; the F positions shift as a consequence. Corrected drawing has a six-membered ring with F meta/para and matches the reference (circle depiction instead of Kekule).

errors_in_wrong_drawing: [substituent_position, high] In the reference the C(=O)NHBn carboxamide is at quinoline C4, next to the ring-fusion carbon. In the wrong drawing the carboxamide is at C3, the carbon adjacent to the NH-bearing C2. | [abbreviation_changed, medium] The reference label NHBn is expanded in the wrong drawing to NH-CH2 with a fully drawn phenyl ring. | [abbreviation_changed, medium] The reference label Me on the tolyl ring (ortho to NH) is written as CH3 in the wrong drawing.
review_notes: Wrong drawing: the carboxamide is at quinoline C3 instead of C4, and Me/NHBn are expanded to CH3 and CH2-phenyl. The corrected drawing restores C4, Me and NHBn. It mixes a circle (pyridine ring) with two Kekule lines (benzo ring) in the quinoline. That still reads as aromatic and was not counted as an error. Transcriber_2's 'wrong' transcription describes an unrelated molecule and was ignored.

errors_in_wrong_drawing: [wrong_atom_or_label, high] The reference has a urea linkage: piperidine N-C(=O)-NH-aryl, with an explicit NH between the carbonyl and the dimethylaminophenyl ring. The wrong drawing replaces that NH with an unlabelled carbon vertex, giving piperidine N-C(=O)-CH2-aryl (an acetamide instead of a urea).
review_notes: Wrong drawing turns the urea NH (between the piperidine carbonyl and the dimethylaminophenyl ring) into a CH2 vertex. Could also be filed as missing_atom_or_group (the NH label is missing). Chain length (10 vertices after Et) matches in all three images. The corrected drawing restores the NH and matches the reference.

errors_in_wrong_drawing: [extra_atom_or_group, high] Reference ether side chain on the aryl ring (ortho to the piperidine attachment) is O-CH2-CH2-NHAc (two carbons); the wrong drawing has O-CH2-CH2-CH2-NHAc (three carbon vertices), adding an extra CH2.
review_notes: Wrong drawing has one extra CH2 in the O-...-NHAc chain (propyl instead of ethyl linker). Corrected drawing has the right two-carbon chain and matches the reference in everything else. Transcriber_2's ref transcription described a different molecule and was ignored.

errors_in_wrong_drawing: [missing_atom_or_group, high] Reference pyrrole N (N7) carries a Me group; in the wrong drawing that N has no substituent, so the N-methyl is missing. | [legibility, low] The hashed wedge from piperidine C3 to Ph is drawn as a detached dense fan of lines that does not clearly join the ring carbon or the Ph label.
review_notes: Wrong drawing omits the Me on the pyrrole N; otherwise the skeleton, I, HO, Boc, Ph and both stereo bonds match. Corrected drawing restores N-Me and matches the reference.
